teile.name: hook
teile.text: Did a kitchen appliance actually create Nike? Bill Bowerman's waffle iron played a part.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game poster style: a 1970s track coach in a warm kitchen presses hot rubber in a waffle iron, steam rising, medium shot, soft morning light, calm space above and below.

teile.name: Waffle Experiment
teile.text: In 1971, Bowerman wanted grip without spikes, so he tested rubber there.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: a fedora-wearing presenter in grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch lifts a waffle iron lid to reveal a rubber sole pattern, close shot, warm kitchen light.

teile.name: Moon Shoe
teile.text: That sole became the 1972 Moon Shoe, then the 1974 Waffle Trainer.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: a runner's shoe sole with deep waffle tread pressing into grass at a 1970s track, low close-up, crisp sunlight, calm sky above.

teile.name: Ultimatum
teile.text: Blue Ribbon Sports sold Tiger shoes. In 1971, Tiger demanded 51 percent.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: two 1970s businessmen face each other across a table in a dim office, one firmly shaking his head, medium shot, tense side lighting.

teile.name: Independent Order
teile.text: So what did they do? They ordered 20,000 shoes, 6,000 with Nike's logo.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: anonymous 1970s workers in a Japanese shoe factory stack boxes of new running shoes, medium wide shot, bright energetic light.

teile.name: Independence
teile.text: Tiger ended in 1972. By 1980, Nike held 50 percent of US athletic shoes.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: wide view of crowded runners in new running shoes on a city street, 1980 era, bright morning light, calm sky above.

teile.name: Abschluss
teile.text: Be sure to like, share and save this video.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: the fedora-wearing presenter in grey suit and dark tie checks his gold pocket watch beside a waffle iron and a running shoe, medium shot, warm light.

entwurf.beschreibung: Nike began as Blue Ribbon Sports in 1964. Bill Bowerman tested rubber in a waffle iron in 1971, and the company later ended its Onitsuka Tiger relationship in 1972.
